曹公歷白檀，破烏丸於柳城

value.outcome: met mountain spirit Yu at this site

sourceDate.text: 秦太子扶蘇北築長城嘗駐此

units.en: Geography Treatise IV — Nanjing Circuit
units.literal: Geography Treatise IV: Nanjing Circuit

units.zh: 南京析津府，本古冀州之地。
units.en: Xijin Prefecture at Nanjing was the old territory of Ji.
units.literal: Nanjing Xijin Prefecture—in ancient times the land of Ji.

units.zh: 高陽氏謂之幽陵，陶唐曰幽都，有虞析為幽州。
units.en: The Gaoyang clan called it Youling; Yao called it Youdu; Shun carved out Youzhou.
units.literal: Gaoyang called it Youling; Taotang Youdu; Shun divided out Youzhou.

units.en: Under Shang, You was folded into Ji.
units.literal: Shang merged You into Ji.

units.en: Zhou reorganized the region once more as You.
units.literal: Zhou divided and rejoined as You.

units.zh: 《職方》，東北幽州，山鎮醫巫閭，澤藪貘養，川河、泲，浸淄、時。
units.en: The Offices of Region record northeast Youzhou with cult mountain Yiwulü, marsh Mo yang, rivers He and Cuo, and the Zi and Shi soaking-in lands.
units.literal: Offices of Region: northeast Youzhou; mountain cult Yiwulü; marsh Mo yang; rivers He, Cuo; soaking Zi, Shi.

units.zh: 其利魚、鹽，其畜馬、牛、豕，其谷黍、稷、稻。
units.en: Its staples were fish and salt; its herds horses, cattle, and pigs; its grains millet, panicum, and rice.
units.literal: Products fish and salt; livestock horses, cattle, swine; grains millet, panicum, rice.

units.en: King Wu enfeoffed the Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.
units.literal: King Wu enfeoffed Grand Guardian Shi in Yan.

units.zh: 秦以其地為漁陽、上谷、右北平、遼西、遼東五郡。
units.en: Qin organized the region into Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong commanderies.
units.literal: Qin made the territory five commanderies: Yuyang, Shanggu, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong.

units.zh: 漢為燕國，歷封臧荼、盧綰、劉建、劉澤、劉旦，嘗置涿郡廣陽國。
units.en: Under Han it became the State of Yan, held in turn by Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, and Liu Dan, with Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State established at intervals.
units.literal: Han made it the State of Yan, successively enfeoffing Zang Tu, Lu Wan, Liu Jian, Liu Ze, Liu Dan; at times Zhuo Commandery and Guangyang State were placed here.

units.zh: 後漢為廣平國廣陽郡，或合於上谷，復置幽州。
units.en: Later Han assigned Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, at times joined to Shanggu; Youzhou was set up again.
units.literal: Later Han made Guangping State and Guangyang Commandery, sometimes merged into Shanggu, then Youzhou was restored.

units.zh: 後周置燕及范陽郡，隋為幽州總管。
units.en: Later Zhou created Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.
units.literal: Later Zhou placed Yan and Fanyang commanderies; Sui made Youzhou a grand protectorate.

units.zh: 唐置大都督府，改范陽節度使。
units.en: Tang installed a metropolitan grand protectorate, later the Fanyang military governor.
units.literal: Tang placed a metropolitan grand protectorate and changed it to the Fanyang military commissioner.

units.zh: 安祿山、史思明、李懷山、朱滔、劉怦、劉濟，相繼割據。
units.en: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, and Liu Ji carved it out one after another.
units.literal: An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Huaishan, Zhu Tao, Liu Peng, Liu Ji seized the region in succession.

units.en: Liu Zong returned to Tang allegiance.
units.literal: Liu Zong submitted to Tang.

units.zh: 至張仲武、張允仲，以正得民。
units.en: Under Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong upright rule won the populace.
units.literal: Through Zhang Zhongwu and Zhang Yunzhong righteousness won the people.

units.zh: 劉仁恭父子僭爭，遂入五代。
units.en: Liu Rengong and his son fought in mutual usurpation until the land entered the Five Dynasties era.
units.literal: Father and son Liu Rengong contended in usurpation, and the region passed into the Five Dynasties.

units.zh: 自唐而晉，高祖以遼有援立之勞，割幽州等十六州以獻。
units.en: When Tang gave way to Jin, Gaozu rewarded Liao for supporting his accession by ceding Youzhou and the other fifteen prefectures.
units.literal: From Tang into Jin, Gaozu, for Liao aid in enthroning him, ceded Youzhou and fifteen other prefectures.

units.zh: 太宗升為南京，又曰燕京。
units.en: Taizong promoted it to Nanjing, also styled Yanjing.
units.literal: Taizong raised it to Nanjing, also called Yanjing.

units.zh: 城方三十六里，崇三丈，衡廣一丈五尺。
units.en: The ramparts formed a thirty-six-li square, three zhang high and one zhang five chi across the top.
units.literal: The wall was thirty-six li square, three zhang high, and one zhang five chi wide on the horizontal face.

units.en: Watchtowers and fighting turrets were fully equipped.
units.literal: Watchtowers and fighting turrets were complete.

units.zh: 八門：東曰安東、迎春，南曰開陽、丹鳳、西曰顯西、清晉、北曰通天、拱辰。
units.en: Eight gates: east—Andong and Yingchun; south—Kaiyang and Danfeng; west—Xianxi and Qingjin; north—Tongtian and Gongchen.
units.literal: Eight gates: east—Andong and Yingchun; south—Kaiyang and Danfeng; west—Xianxi and Qingjin; north—Tongtian and Gongchen.

units.en: The inner palace stood in the southwest corner.
units.literal: The inner palace was in the southwest corner.

units.zh: 皇城內有景宗、聖宗御容殿二，東曰宣和，南曰大內。
units.en: Inside the imperial city stood two portrait halls of Jingzong and Shengzong; the east was Xuanhe, the south the Inner Palace.
units.literal: Within the imperial city were two portrait halls of Jingzong and Shengzong; east was Xuanhe, south the Inner Palace.

units.en: The inner gate was Xuanjiao, renamed Yuanhe;
units.literal: The inner gate was Xuanjiao, renamed Yuanhe;

units.zh: 外三門曰南端、左掖、右掖。
units.en: the three outer gates were the south end, left flank, and right flank.
units.literal: the outer three gates were the south end, left flank, and right flank.

units.zh: 左掖改萬春，右掖改千秋。
units.en: The left flank became Wanchun; the right flank became Qianqiu.
units.literal: The left flank was renamed Wanchun; the right flank Qianqiu.

units.zh: 門有樓閣，球場在其南，東為永平館。
units.en: Gate-towers crowned the gates; the ball court lay to the south, and Yongping Hostel to the east.
units.literal: The gates had tower-pavilions; the ball court lay south of them; east was Yongping Hostel.

units.zh: 皇城西門曰顯西，設而不開；
units.en: The imperial city's west gate was Xianxi, built but never opened;
units.literal: The imperial city west gate was Xianxi, built but not opened;

units.en: the north gate was Zibei.
units.literal: north was Zibei.

units.zh: 西城巔有涼殿，東北隅有燕角樓。
units.en: A cool hall crowned the west rampart; Yanjiao Tower stood in the northeast corner.
units.literal: On the west rampart summit was a cool hall; in the northeast corner was Yanjiao Tower.

units.zh: 坊市、廨舍、寺觀，蓋不勝書。
units.en: Wards, markets, offices, and temples were beyond full reckoning.
units.literal: Wards, markets, offices, and temples—too many to record.

units.zh: 其外，有居庸、松亭、榆林之關。
units.en: Beyond the walls lay the passes of Juyong, Songting, and Yulin.
units.literal: Outside were the passes of Juyong, Songting, and Yulin.

units.zh: 古北之口，桑乾河、高梁河、石子河、大安山、燕山，中有瑤嶼。
units.en: At Gubei Pass flowed the Sanggan, Gaoliang, and Shizi rivers; Daan Mountain and the Yan range rose there, with Yaoyu isle among them.
units.literal: At Gubei mouth were the Sanggan, Gaoliang, and Shizi rivers, Daan Mountain, the Yan Mountains, and amid them Yaoyu isle.

units.zh: 府曰幽都，軍號盧龍，開泰元年落軍額。
units.en: The prefecture was called Youdu, with the army title Lulong; in the first year of Kaitai, the army designation was abolished.
units.literal: The prefecture was called Youdu; its army title was Lulong. In the first year of Kaitai, the army designation was dropped.

units.en: It governed six prefectures and eleven counties: Xijin County.
units.literal: Governing six prefectures and eleven counties: Xijin County.

units.zh: 本晉薊縣，改薊北縣，開泰元年更今名。
units.en: Formerly Jin Jixian and then Jibei County, it took its present name in the first year of Kaitai.
units.literal: Originally Jin Jixian, it was changed to Jibei County; in the first year of Kaitai it received the present name.

units.zh: 以燕分野旅寅為析木之津，故名。
units.en: Named for Yan's astral field at Lüyin, the ford of Ximu.
units.literal: Because Yan's astral allotment lies at Lüyin as the ford of Ximu, it was so named.

units.en: Twenty thousand registered households.
units.literal: Twenty thousand households.

units.en: Wanping County.
units.literal: Wanping County.

units.zh: 本晉幽都縣，開泰元年改今名。
units.en: Formerly Jin Youdu County, it took its present name in the first year of Kaitai.
units.literal: Originally Jin Youdu County, it was changed to the present name in the first year of Kaitai.

units.en: Twenty-two thousand registered households.
units.literal: Twenty-two thousand households.

units.en: Changping County.
units.literal: Changping County.

units.zh: 本漢軍都縣，後漢屬廣陽郡，晉屬燕國，元魏置東燕州、平昌郡及昌平縣。
units.en: It was Han Jundu County; Later Han Guangyang Commandery; Jin Yan State; Northern Wei founded Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.
units.literal: Originally Han Jundu County; Later Han belonged to Guangyang Commandery; Jin to Yan State; Northern Wei set Eastern Yan Prefecture, Pingchang Commandery, and Changping County.

units.en: When the commandery was abolished the county answered to Youzhou.
units.literal: Commandery abolished; county subordinated to Youzhou.

units.en: It lay ninety li north of the capital.
units.literal: Ninety li north of the capital.

units.en: Seven thousand registered households.
units.literal: Seven thousand households.

units.en: Liangxiang County.
units.literal: Liangxiang County.

units.zh: 燕為中都縣，漢改良鄉縣，舊屬涿郡，北齊天保七年省入薊縣，武平六年復置。
units.en: Under Yan it was Zhongdu County; Han renamed it Liangxiang in Zhuo Commandery; Northern Qi Tianbao year 7 merged it into Jixian, restored Wuping year 6.
units.literal: Under Yan it was Zhongdu County; Han changed it to Liangxiang County, formerly in Zhuo Commandery; Northern Qi Tianbao year 7 merged it into Jixian, Wuping year 6 restored it.

units.zh: 唐聖歷元年改固節鎮，神龍元年復為良鄉縣，劉守光徙治此。
units.en: In the first year of Tang Shengli it became Gujie Fort; in the first year of Shenlong, Liangxiang County was restored; Liu Shouguang moved the administration here.
units.literal: In the first year of Tang Shengli it was changed to Gujie Fort; in the first year of Shenlong, Liangxiang County was restored; Liu Shouguang moved the seat here.

units.en: Sixty li from Nanjing.
units.literal: Sixty li from Nanjing.

units.en: Seven thousand registered households.
units.literal: Seven thousand households.

units.en: Lu County.
units.literal: Lu County.

units.en: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.
units.literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德二年置元州，貞觀元年州廢，復為縣。
units.en: Tang Wude year 2 created Yuan Prefecture; in Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished and the county restored.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 2 set Yuan Prefecture; in the first year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and it again became a county.

units.en: The Lu River flows there.
units.literal: There is the Lu River.

units.en: It stood sixty li east of the capital.
units.literal: Sixty li east of the capital.

units.en: Six thousand registered households.
units.literal: Six thousand households.

units.en: Anji County.
units.literal: Anji County.

units.en: Formerly a Han county in Yuyang Commandery.
units.literal: Originally a Han county, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德四年徙置東南五十里石梁城，貞觀八年又徙今縣西五里常道城，開元二十三年又徙耿就橋行市南。
units.en: In Tang Wude year 4 the seat shifted fifty li southeast to Shiliang town; Zhenguan year 8 to Changdao town five li west of the present site; Kaiyuan year 23 to the market south of Gengjiu Bridge.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 4 moved fifty li southeast to Shiliang walled town; Zhenguan year 8 again moved five li west of the present county to Changdao walled town; Kaiyuan year 23 again moved south of Gengjiu Bridge market.

units.en: It lay one hundred twenty li south of the capital.
units.literal: One hundred twenty li south of the capital.

units.en: Twelve thousand registered households.
units.literal: Twelve thousand households.

units.en: Yongqing County.
units.literal: Yongqing County.

units.zh: 本漢益昌縣，隋置通澤縣，唐置武隆縣，改會昌，天寶初為永清縣。
units.en: It was Han Yichang County; Sui Tongze County; Tang Wulong, then Huichang; at the opening of Tianbao it was renamed Yongqing.
units.literal: Originally Han Yichang County; Sui set Tongze County; Tang set Wulong County, renamed Huichang; at the start of Tianbao it became Yongqing County.

units.en: It stood one hundred fifty li south of the capital.
units.literal: One hundred fifty li south of the capital.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.en: Wuqing County.
units.literal: Wuqing County.

units.en: Former Han Yongnu County in Yuyang Commandery.
units.literal: Former Han Yongnu County, belonging to Yuyang Commandery.

units.zh: 《水經註》，雍奴者，藪澤之名，四面有水曰雍，不流曰奴。
units.en: The Water Classic commentary explains Yongnu as a marsh name: water on four sides is yong; stagnant water is nu.
units.literal: Commentary on the Water Classic: Yongnu is the name of a marsh-lake; water on four sides is yong; water that does not flow is nu.

units.en: At the opening of Tang Tianbao it was renamed Wuqing.
units.literal: At the start of Tang Tianbao it was changed to Wuqing.

units.en: It lay one hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.
units.literal: One hundred fifty li southeast of the capital.

units.en: Ten thousand registered households.
units.literal: Ten thousand households.

units.en: Xianghe County.
units.literal: Xianghe County.

units.en: Formerly Sun Village in Wuqing.
units.literal: Originally Sun Village in Wuqing.

units.zh: 遼於新倉置榷鹽院，居民聚集，因分武清、三河、潞三縣戶置。
units.en: The Liao founded a salt monopoly at Xincang; settlers clustered there, and households were carved from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu to form the county.
units.literal: Liao placed a salt monopoly office at Xincang; residents gathered; households were split from Wuqing, Sanhe, and Lu counties to establish it.

units.en: It stood one hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.
units.literal: One hundred twenty li southeast of the capital.

units.en: Seven thousand registered households.
units.literal: Seven thousand households.

units.en: Yuhe County.
units.literal: Yuhe County.

units.en: Formerly Quanshan land.
units.literal: Originally Quanshan territory.

units.zh: 劉仁恭於大安山創宮觀，師煉丹羽化之術於方士王若訥，因割薊縣分置，以供給之。
units.en: Liu Rengong erected palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain and studied alchemy and immortal arts from the fangshi Wang Ruone; he therefore detached part of Jixian to provision them.
units.literal: Liu Rengong built palaces and shrines on Daan Mountain; he studied elixir and ascension arts under the fangshi Wang Ruone; he therefore split off Jixian to supply them.

units.en: It lay forty li west of the capital.
units.literal: Forty li west of the capital.

units.en: One thousand registered households.
units.literal: One thousand households.

units.en: Huoyin County.
units.literal: Huoyin County.

units.en: Formerly Huo Village in Han Quanshan.
units.literal: Originally Huo Village in Han Quanshan.

units.zh: 遼每季春，弋獵於延芳澱，居民成邑，就城故漷陰鎮，後改為縣。
units.en: Each spring the Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; settlers formed a town around the old Huoyin fort, later raised to a county.
units.literal: Each spring Liao hunted at Yanfang Marsh; residents formed a town; the old Huoyin walled town was walled, later changed to a county.

units.en: It stood ninety li southeast of the capital.
units.literal: Ninety li southeast of the capital.

units.zh: 延芳澱方數百里，春時鵝鶩所聚，夏秋多菱芡。
units.en: Yanfang Marsh covers hundreds of li; spring brings geese and ducks; summer and autumn yield water chestnuts and lotus.
units.literal: Yanfang Marsh spans several hundred li; in spring geese and ducks gather; in summer and autumn many water chestnuts and lotus roots grow.

units.zh: 國主春獵，衛士皆衣墨綠，各持連鎚、鷹食、刺鵝錐，列水次，相去五七步。
units.en: For the spring hunt guards wore dark green, spaced five or seven paces along the shore with linked maces, hawk bait, and goose awls.
units.literal: When the ruler hunted in spring, guards all wore dark green, each holding linked maces, hawk food, and goose-stabbing awls, lined along the water five or seven paces apart.

units.zh: 上風擊鼓，驚鵝稍離水面。
units.en: Drums upwind startled geese to lift slightly from the water.
units.literal: Upwind they beat drums to startle geese slightly from the water.

units.zh: 國主親放海東青鶻擒之。
units.en: The ruler himself flew eastern-sea green goshawks to take them.
units.literal: The ruler personally loosed eastern-sea green goshawks to seize them.

units.zh: 鵝墜，恐鶻力不勝，在列者以佩錐刺鵝，急取其臘飼鶻。
units.en: If a goose fell and the hawk might fail, men in line stabbed it with belt awls and hurriedly took its fat for the hawk.
units.literal: When a goose fell, fearing the hawk lacked strength, those in line stabbed the goose with belt awls and swiftly took its fat to feed the hawk.

units.en: Capturing the lead goose brought a standard reward of silver and silk.
units.literal: Whoever took the lead goose received silver and silk by rule.

units.zh: 國主、皇族、群臣各有分地。
units.en: The ruler, imperial kin, and ministers each held assigned hunting grounds.
units.literal: Ruler, imperial clan, and ministers each had allotted grounds.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.zh: 宋王曾《上契丹事》曰：「自雄州白溝驛渡河，四十里至新城縣，古督亢亭之地。
units.en: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: "From Xiongzhou's Baigou post, forty li by ferry to Xincheng County, the old Dukang Pavilion site.
units.literal: Song minister Wang Zeng, Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan, says: "From Xiongzhou Baigou post one crosses the river; forty li to Xincheng County, ancient Dukang Pavilion ground.

units.en: Seventy li farther on lies Zhuo Prefecture.
units.literal: Another seventy li to Zhuo Prefecture.

units.zh: 北渡範水、劉李河，六十里至良鄉縣。
units.en: Crossing the Fan and Liu-Li rivers northward, sixty li to Liangxiang County.
units.literal: Northward crossing Fan River and Liu-Li River, sixty li to Liangxiang County.

units.zh: 渡盧溝河，六十里至幽州，號燕京。
units.en: Sixty li beyond the Lugou River stands Youzhou, called Yanjing.
units.literal: Crossing Lugou River, sixty li to Youzhou, styled Yanjing.

units.en: The inner city hugged the southwest of the outer ramparts.
units.literal: The inner city was built against the outer wall's southwest.

units.zh: 正南曰啟夏門，內有元和殿，東門曰宣和。
units.en: The south gate is Qixia; inside stands Yuanhe Hall; the east gate is Xuanhe.
units.literal: Due south is Qixia Gate; within is Yuanhe Hall; east gate is Xuanhe.

units.en: Every ward and lane in the city had gate-towers.
units.literal: Within the city every ward lane had towers.

units.zh: 有閔忠寺，本唐太宗為征遼陣亡將士所造；
units.en: Minzhong Temple, which Tang Taizong raised for officers and men fallen on the Liaodong campaign;
units.literal: There is Minzhong Temple, originally built by Tang Taizong for generals and soldiers who died campaigning against Liaodong;

units.zh: 又有開泰寺，魏王耶律漢寧造。
units.en: and Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.
units.literal: also Kaitai Temple, built by Prince of Wei Yelü Hanning.

units.en: Court envoys were sent to tour both.
units.literal: Both were sent envoys from the court to visit.

units.zh: 南門外有於越王廨，為宴集之所。
units.en: Outside the south gate was the Yuyue Prince's office, a place for banquets.
units.literal: Outside the south gate was the Yuyue Prince's office, a place for banquets.

units.zh: 門外永平館，舊名碣石館，請和後易之。
units.en: Beyond the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace accord.
units.literal: Outside the gate is Yongping Hostel, formerly named Jieshi Hostel, renamed after the peace treaty.

units.en: South lies the Sanggan River."
units.literal: South of it is the Sanggan River."

units.en: Shun Prefecture—Guihua Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Shun Prefecture, Guihua Army, middle grade, cishi.

units.zh: 秦上谷，漢范陽，北齊歸德郡境。
units.en: In Qin it was Shanggu; in Han Fanyang; in Northern Qi part of Guidde Commandery.
units.literal: Qin Shanggu; Han Fanyang; Northern Qi Guidde Commandery territory.

units.zh: 隋開皇中，粟末靺鞨與高麗戰不勝，厥稽部長突地稽率八部勝兵數千人，自扶餘城西北舉落內附，置順州以處之。
units.en: Under Sui Kaihuang, Sumo Mohe lost to Goryeo; Jueji chief Tudi led several thousand warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu to submit, and Shun Prefecture was founded to receive them.
units.literal: Sui Kaihuang era: Sumo Mohe fought Goryeo without victory; chief Tudi of the Jueji tribe led several thousand victorious warriors of eight tribes from northwest of Fuyu walled city to submit inward; Shun Prefecture was set to settle them.

units.zh: 唐武德初改燕州，會昌中改歸順州，唐末仍為順州。
units.en: Early Tang Wude renamed it Yan Prefecture; in Huichang it became Guishun; by late Tang it was again Shun Prefecture.
units.literal: Tang early Wude changed it to Yan Prefecture; Huichang era changed to Guishun Prefecture; late Tang it remained Shun Prefecture.

units.en: It has the Wanyu and Baisui rivers;
units.literal: There are Wanyu River and Baisui River;

units.zh: 曹王山，曹操嘗駐軍於此，黍谷山，鄒衍吹律之地，南有齊長城。

units.en: Formerly Han Lingzhi County land, long defunct.
units.literal: Originally Han Lingzhi County territory, long abolished.

units.zh: 太祖以定州安喜縣俘戶置。
units.en: Taizu founded it with captives from Ding Prefecture's Anxi County.
units.literal: Taizu settled it with captive households from Ding Prefecture Anxi County.

units.en: Sixty li northeast of the prefectural seat.
units.literal: Sixty li northeast of the prefecture.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.en: Wangdu County.
units.literal: Wangdu County.

units.en: Formerly Han Haiyang County, long defunct.
units.literal: Originally Han Haiyang County, long abolished.

units.zh: 太祖以定州望都縣俘戶置。
units.en: Taizu founded it with captives from Ding Prefecture's Wangdu County.
units.literal: Taizu settled it with captive households from Ding Prefecture Wangdu County.

units.en: Haiyang Mountain stands there.
units.literal: There is Haiyang Mountain.

units.zh: 縣在州南三十里，戶三千。
units.en: The county lies thirty li south of the prefectural seat; three thousand households.
units.literal: County thirty li south of the prefecture; three thousand households.

units.en: Luan Prefecture—Yong'an Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Luan Prefecture, Yong'an Army, middle grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly the old Huangluo walled town.
units.literal: Originally ancient Huangluo walled city.

units.en: The Luan River rings it below Lulong Mountain.
units.literal: Luan River encircles it south of Lulong Mountain.

units.zh: 齊桓公伐山戎，見山神俞，即此。
units.en: When Duke Huan of Qi attacked the Mountain Rong he met the mountain spirit Yu—this is that place.
units.literal: Qi Duke Huan campaigned against the Mountain Rong and saw the mountain spirit Yu—this is that place.

units.en: Under Qin it was Youbeiping.
units.literal: Qin made Youbeiping.

units.zh: 漢為石城縣，後名海陽縣。
units.en: Han founded Shicheng County, later Haiyang County.
units.literal: Han made Shicheng County, later named Haiyang County.

units.en: In late Han Gongsun Du held it.
units.literal: Late Han it belonged to Gongsun Du.

units.en: After Jin it lay in Liaoxi.
units.literal: After Jin it belonged to Liaoxi.

units.en: When Later Jin ceded land it fell within Ping Prefecture.
units.literal: Later Jin ceded territory; it lay within Ping Prefecture.

units.en: Taizu founded it with war captives.
units.literal: Taizu settled it with captive households.

units.zh: 灤州負山帶河，為朔漢形勝之地。
units.en: Luan Prefecture lies against mountains and rivers, a strategic hinge between the northern marches and the Han heartland.
units.literal: Luan Prefecture backs mountains and embraces rivers—a strategic place between the northern frontiers and Han lands.

units.zh: 有扶蘇泉，甚甘美，秦太子扶蘇北築長城嘗駐此；
units.en: Fusu Spring, exceedingly sweet, where Qin crown prince Fusu camped while raising the northern Long Wall;
units.literal: There is Fusu Spring, very sweet; Qin crown prince Fusu, while building the Long Wall in the north, once encamped here;

units.zh: 臨榆山，峰巒崛起，高千餘仞，下臨渝河。
units.en: Linyu Mountain rises in sheer peaks over a thousand ren, looking down on the Yu River.
units.literal: Linyu Mountain, peaks soaring more than a thousand ren high, overlooking the Yu River below.

units.en: It governed three counties: Yifeng County.
units.literal: Governing three counties: Yifeng County.

units.en: Formerly the old Huangluo town.
units.literal: Originally Huangluo old walled city.

units.zh: 黃洛水北出盧龍山，南流入於濡水。
units.en: Huangluo River issues north from Lulong Mountain and runs south into the Ru River.
units.literal: Huangluo River emerges north from Lulong Mountain and flows south into Ru River.

units.en: Under Han it was Liaoxi Commandery, long defunct.
units.literal: Han belonged to Liaoxi Commandery, long abolished.

units.en: Late Tang it passed to the Khitan; Shizong founded the county.
units.literal: Late Tang entered Khitan rule; Shizong established the county.

units.en: Four thousand registered households.
units.literal: Four thousand households.

units.en: Macheng County.
units.literal: Macheng County.

units.en: Formerly Lulong County land.
units.literal: Originally Lulong County territory.

units.zh: 唐開元二十八年析置縣，以通水運。
units.en: Tang Kaiyuan year 28 carved out a county to facilitate river transport.
units.literal: Tang Kaiyuan year 28 split off a county to open water transport.

units.zh: 東北有千金冶，東有茂鄉鎮。
units.en: Northeast lies Qianjin smeltery; east, Maoxiang town.
units.literal: Northeast is Qianjin smeltery; east is Maoxiang walled town.

units.en: The Liao detached it to Luan Prefecture.
units.literal: Liao split it off to belong to Luan Prefecture.

units.en: Forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
units.literal: Forty li southwest of the prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Shicheng County.
units.literal: Shicheng County.

units.en: Han founded it in Youbeiping Commandery, long defunct.
units.literal: Han established it, belonging to Youbeiping Commandery, long abolished.

units.zh: 唐貞觀中於此置臨渝縣，萬歲通天元年改石城縣，在灤州南三十里，唐儀鳳石刻在焉。
units.en: Tang Zhenguan placed Linyu County here; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian renamed it Shicheng, thirty li south of Luan Prefecture, where a Tang Yifeng inscription remains.
units.literal: Tang Zhenguan era placed Linyu County here; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian changed to Shicheng County, thirty li south of Luan Prefecture; Tang Yifeng stone inscription stands there.

units.zh: 今縣又在其南五十里，遼徙置以就鹽官。
units.en: The present seat lies fifty li farther south; the Liao relocated it beside the salt monopoly.
units.literal: Present county again fifty li farther south; Liao moved the seat to approach the salt office.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Ying Prefecture—Linhai Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Ying Prefecture, Linhai Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly the Shang Guzhu state.
units.literal: Originally the Shang Guzhu state.

units.en: Under Qin it lay in Liaoxi Commandery.
units.literal: Qin belonged to Liaoxi Commandery.

units.en: Han made it Changli Commandery.
units.literal: Han made it Changli Commandery.

units.en: Former Yan's Murong Huang moved the capital here.
units.literal: Former Yan Murong Huang moved the capital here.

units.zh: 元魏立營州，領昌黎、建德、遼東、樂浪、冀陽、營丘六郡。
units.en: Northern Wei founded Ying Prefecture over Changli, Jiande, Liaodong, Lelang, Jiyang, and Yingqiu commanderies.
units.literal: Northern Wei set Ying Prefecture, governing Changli, Jiande, Liaodong, Lelang, Jiyang, and Yingqiu six commanderies.

units.en: Later Zhou it was held by Gao Baoning.
units.literal: Later Zhou was seized by Gao Baoning.

units.zh: 隋開皇置州，大業改遼西郡。
units.en: Sui Kaihuang established the prefecture; Daye made it Liaoxi Commandery.
units.literal: Sui Kaihuang set the prefecture; Daye changed it to Liaoxi Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德元年改營州，萬歲通天元年始入契丹。
units.en: In the first year of Tang Wude, Ying Prefecture was restored; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian, it first passed to the Khitan.
units.literal: In the first year of Tang Wude, it was changed to Ying Prefecture; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian, it first fell to the Khitan.

units.en: Shengli year 2 the seat was by proxy at Yuyang.
units.literal: Shengli year 2 administered by proxy at Yuyang.

units.en: Kaiyuan year 5 the administration returned to Liucheng.
units.literal: Kaiyuan year 5 the seat returned to Liucheng.

units.en: Tianbao year 1 it became Liucheng Commandery.
units.literal: Tianbao year 1 changed to Liucheng Commandery.

units.en: Later Tang restored Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Later Tang restored Ying Prefecture.

units.en: Taizu placed Ding Prefecture captives there.
units.literal: Taizu settled Ding Prefecture captive households there.

units.en: It governed one county: Guangning County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Guangning County.

units.en: Formerly Han Liucheng County in Liaoxi Commandery.
units.literal: Han Liucheng County, belonging to Liaoxi Commandery.

units.en: To the northeast it bordered the Xi and Khitan.
units.literal: Northeast it bordered the Xi and Khitan.

units.zh: 萬歲通天元年，入契丹李萬榮。
units.en: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, it fell to the Khitan Li Wanrong.
units.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, it fell to the Khitan Li Wanrong.

units.en: Shenlong year 1 the seat shifted to the Youzhou border.
units.literal: Shenlong year 1 the seat moved to the Youzhou border.

units.en: Kaiyuan year 4 restored the former territory.
units.literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored the old territory.

units.en: The Liao gave it the present name.
units.literal: Liao changed to the present name.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.
